entries.claim: Task 6 commits a user-visible installer change (CloseApplications=force) on its own, with no CHANGELOG.md entry. The entry lands only later, in Task 7's commit. That breaks the repo rule that every user-visible change lands with its [Unreleased] entry in the same commit (CLAUDE.md changelog binding, CONTRIBUTING.md:33).
entries.failure_scenario: Executor commits Task 6 alone, as the plan's per-task commits and Task 7's 'This is the phase's last commit' imply. That commit force-closes a running HQPTuner.exe and adds a Preparing page to interactive installs, but CHANGELOG.md is not touched. The commit then breaks the same-commit changelog rule, and Task 7's sentence 'the fix and its entry land together' is true only of half the fix.

entries.claim: Task 1 does not say where the v1.20.1 installer is downloaded. The smoke step passes the unquoted glob `dist/*-setup.exe` (release.yml smoke-windows matrix `target`), and the obvious choice, `gh release download --dir dist`, makes that glob match two installers.
entries.failure_scenario: HQPTuner-1.20.1-setup.exe goes into dist/ next to the new HQPTuner-X-setup.exe. `bash packaging/windows/smoke.sh dist/*-setup.exe x64 --signed <prev>` then expands to extra positional arguments, so smoke.sh's argument check (`[ $# -eq 2 ] || [ $# -eq 3 ]` today, or its Task 1 successor) dies with usage, or takes the old installer as TARGET. The red push then fails before any upgrade step. Task 5 says that does not count as the bite proof, so one owner push is wasted. The plan sets no rule against this, such as a separate download directory or a non-glob target.
